title: Milestone 2: DynamoDB-powered internal bot boards with S3 canonical records
description:
Outcome: bots have durable internal boards and to-do lists separate from the project boards on their computers. A bot can track ongoing work without creating or borrowing a project repository board.

Storage direction requested by Ryan: cloud Kanbus/Virtuus approach with canonical issue files/text on S3 and DynamoDB card-catalog indexes powering internal boards. DynamoDB supplies scoped discovery/query indexes; S3 holds canonical record content. This is a proposed integration, not a claim that Kanbus/Virtuus already provides a ready Chatticus backend. A local project board remains file-based under Milestone 1; this milestone does not silently migrate it.

Definition of Done: internal boards remain distinct from project boards; approved agent and user flows operate within the selected board scope; canonical records and indexes have specified consistency/recovery behavior; shared @kanbus/ui components remain DRY and themeable across both stores. Specify behavior before product code and prove the selected backend's capabilities before relying on them.

Open questions: one board per bot, user, organization or another scope? Which account owns canonical objects/indexes, and what authorizes access? Which tools can run without summoning a computer? Which users see or edit which internal lists? How do writes, retries, concurrent updates, catalog lag and index rebuilding work without reporting false success? How does this relate to the historical thin Task item and its evidence-to-complete rule? Decide through design/acceptance review, not by assuming a table/key/API/IAM scheme or migration.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Owner decisions, 2026-10-20 (Ryan): (1) One internal board per bot, kept within its organization; per-user and per-organization lists may come later. (2) Bots use Kanbus for their work tracking: the bot's Kanbus board REPLACES the existing thin Task items (task tool create/get/complete/close, DynamoDB task records, web task list) as a hard cutover with a one-time migration of existing items; the evidence-to-complete rule carries over as a board rule (a card moves to Done only with evidence). (3) Storage per the existing direction: canonical record on S3 in the Kanbus issue JSON format, DynamoDB index for lookup, in the Chatticus production account, isolated per environment and per organization; the same Kanbus parser and @kanbus/ui component serve project boards and bot boards. (4) Access only through the Chatticus front door with organization membership checks; bots through a tool; computers never touch the store. (5) Bot board tools run without summoning the computer. (6) Members who can see the bot can see its board; the bot and the organization's owners and admins edit; other members read-only to start. (7) Conditional writes per card update, idempotent retries, honest saving and failed states, visible index lag, and an index rebuild from the S3 records. (8) Same Board tab with a picker: Project boards (on the computer) and Bot boards. Before any design detail: check with the Kanbus project whether Kanbus or Virtuus already has a cloud issue store to reuse, so Chatticus does not build a parallel one; then write the Gherkin first.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Owner decisions on storage, 2026-10-20 (Ryan), after the Kanbus project reported that a Kanbus/Virtuus cloud store already exists in Preview (virtuus-store crate: S3 canonical Kanbus JSON plus a rebuildable DynamoDB catalog, conditional writes by revision, operation ids for idempotent retries, catalog_pending on lag; kanbus-api: axum service and Lambda behind API Gateway, used by Prospectus): (1) Kanbus owns the cloud store and its API; Chatticus consumes it and designs no store of its own. (2) Chatticus deploys Kanbus's own kanbus-api unchanged in the Chatticus production account, one per environment, and the TypeScript control plane calls it. (3) Mapping of one board per bot: the cleanest, most elegant Kanbus-native model; pending the Kanbus project's answer on the 8-project limit (candidate: one Kanbus project per bot, tenant = organization id). (4) Building on Preview is fine, development first. Needs filed with the Kanbus project: deployable artifact with a per-environment layout, service-to-service auth, a TypeScript client, parent and dependency writes through the API, and whatever the per-bot mapping requires.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decision 2026-10-20: one Kanbus project per bot (tenant = Chatticus organization id, project = bot id, one bucket and table per environment) as the cleanest Kanbus-native model (Ryan asked for the cleanest and most elegant way; the Kanbus project recommends it). The 8-project cap in kanbus-api is a Preview query budget, not a storage limit. Blocking dependency on the Kanbus side: the shipped kanbus-api Lambda serves one tenant/project fixed at deploy time. Kanbus epic kbs-f4ecb4a8 tracks: kbs-9cb5cb40 per-request tenant/project from verified identity (blocking), kbs-494ecd64 query budget instead of a project cap, kbs-4818904b deployable artifact and CDK construct per environment, kbs-f222b6ee service-to-service auth, kbs-a19d1443 TypeScript client, kbs-8283b923 parent and dependency writes; plus kbs-460415fd pure parsers for the offline project view. Chatticus writes behavior specs now and builds no code against kanbus-api until those land.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decisions of 2026-10-20 applied to the spec (PR 622). Owner: (a) only owners edit a board, no admin role; (b) every member who can see the bot reads its board; (c) org-wide all-bots view wanted later, not a priority, not built now (will use GET /{tenant}/api/issues?projects=a,b, kbs-494ecd64); (d) unplaceable Task items reported to owners, deleted after an owner has seen the report; (e) bots close, never delete; owners may delete; (f) deleted bot -> board archived, restorable, purged after 30 days, owner may request immediate removal. Kanbus: (g) board provisioned with Kanbus default config (PUT config, empty body), statuses backlog/open/in_progress/blocked/closed; (h) one closed status, closing comment + custom.closing completed|abandoned, reopen allowed; (i) service principal + X-Kanbus-Actor chatticus:user|bot:<uuid>; (j) board in the path, 403 for ungranted, one deployment per environment, tenant=org uuid, project=bot uuid; (k) stories kbs-9cb5cb40, 494ecd64, 4818904b, f222b6ee, a19d1443, 8283b923, 344f42ca, 791a7373, 460415fd.

right_now_summary: The team is defining access, consistency, and isolation rules before integrating S3 and DynamoDB.
